# polylane_workspace (Resource)

Adopts an existing Polylane workspace so its safe, non-secret properties can be managed with Terraform. Workspaces must be imported; this resource does not create or delete them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "polylane_workspace" "current" {
  # Workspaces are adopted by import. Add name, slug, description, or
  # auto_join only when Terraform should manage that property.
}

import {
  to = polylane_workspace.current
  id = "ws_00000000000000000000000000000000"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `auto_join` (Boolean) Whether verified users with the workspace email domain can join automatically.
- `description` (String) Workspace description.
- `name` (String) Human-readable workspace name.
- `slug` (String) URL-friendly workspace slug.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp when the workspace was created.
- `domain` (String) Email domain claimed by the workspace, if any.
- `id` (String) Unique Polylane workspace ID.
- `owner_id` (String) ID of the workspace owner.
- `updated_at` (String) RFC 3339 timestamp when the workspace was last updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import polylane_workspace.current ws_00000000000000000000000000000000
```
